title: What movement takes you from 2 to -3?
description: The movement from two to negative three is found in two ways. The first counts the steps on the number line and writes target take away start. The second cuts the walk at zero and adds the two movements. Keeko's doubt is that the movement is positive.
teaching_notes: One idea: the movement from two to negative three is the target take away the start, and the same total comes from cutting the walk at zero. Watch for students who take the target away from the start and get the wrong sign.

source: If we start at 2 and wish to go to -3, what is the movement needed?
video_script.why: The child finds the movement between two numbers as target take away start, and sees the same movement as a sum of two movements through zero.
video_script.substitution: The book's own walk on the number line from two to negative three, solved in two ways.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book, with a walker going from two to negative three
video_script.wrong_move: takes the target away from the start, two take away negative three, and gets the opposite sign
video_script.payoff_line: The movement needed is negative five.

final_answer.spoken: the movement needed is negative five

maths_rules: movement needed = target number - starting number
first way: -3 - 2 = -5; the walker goes 5 steps backward
second way: from 2 to 0 is 0 - 2 = -2; from 0 to -3 is -3 - 0 = -3
total movement = (-3) + (-2) = -5; this sum has no take away
slip: 2 - (-3) = 5 is start take away target, and +5 from 2 reaches 7, not -3
video_script.design: The number line from -10 to 10 with a walker on 2; the walk to -3 is shown whole, then cut at zero.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the number line from -10 to 10 with a walker on 2 and -3 lit up

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the number line is drawn
marks.ask: the number -3 lights up and a question mark appears between them

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the number line.
<bookmark mark='walker'/>We start at two and wish to go to negative three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the movement needed to get from one to the other?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Target number - Starting number = Movement needed;  Target number = Starting number + Movement needed

marks.rule: the two lines are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The movement needed is the target number take away the starting number.
The target is the start plus the movement.

marks.given: the start and the target are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the starting number is two, and the target number is negative three.

marks.find: the words movement needed are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the movement needed.

beats.on_screen: look at the line: 5 steps backward;  -3 - 2 = -5

marks.walk: the walker steps left from 2 to -3 and the count 1 to 5 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='walk'/>Step one, look at the number line, where the walker goes five steps backward.
<bookmark mark='take'/>As a take away, negative three take away two is negative five.

marks.cut: the walk is cut at 0 into two parts
marks.first: the first part from 2 to 0 is marked and 0 - 2 = -2 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step two, cut the walk at zero, into two parts.
<bookmark mark='first'/>From two to zero, the movement is zero take away two, which is negative two.

marks.second: the second part from 0 to -3 is marked and -3 - 0 = -3 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step three, now the walk from zero to negative three. The movement is negative three take away zero, which is negative three.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total is negative three plus negative two, and that is negative five. This sum has no take away.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The movement needed is -5;  check 2 + (-5) = -3
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Both ways give the same answer.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The movement needed is negative five.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 2 - (-3) = 5 shown with the walker jumping from 2 to 7; struck out

marks.doubt: 2 - (-3) = 5 is written and the walker jumps right to 7
marks.fix: the jump is struck out and the walker returns to 2
marks.why: the arrow from 2 to -3 lights up on the left

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the movement is positive five, because two take away negative three is five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But positive five from two reaches seven, not negative three.
<bookmark mark='why'/>That took the target away from the start, but the target must come first.
